analysis.investment_thesis: Nesco is a high-quality, near-monopoly asset (Bombay Exhibition Centre + IT Park on prime Mumbai land) with exceptional 50%+ operating margins and negligible debt, but revenue growth is decelerating sharply to ~8% in FY25 and the PEG of ~1.7x (using 9Y earnings CAGR of 12%) is too stretched for a GARP buyer. The FY25 capex surge of ₹784 Cr (vs ₹105 Cr prior year) is the real story — if the expansion drives reacceleration to 20%+ earnings growth, this re-rates significantly; if not, it's a stalwart priced like a grower.
key_strengths: Near-monopoly exhibition venue in Mumbai with 50.87% operating margins — this kind of pricing power is extraordinary and visible from the street
Balance sheet fortress: D/E of just 0.04 and ₹2,785 Cr in reserves; the ₹761 Cr CWIP signals self-funded expansion without dilution
High-conviction promoter skin in the game at 68.54% holding — they're not selling, they're building
key_risks: Revenue growth decelerated hard — from 24% in FY24 to just 8% in FY25 (₹678 Cr → ₹732 Cr); if this is structural, not cyclical, the story breaks
Conglomerate diworsification: shot blasting machines + food courts + exhibition halls + IT parks = Lynch's nightmare, each segment diluting focus
Free cash flow turned deeply negative (−₹435 Cr in FY25) due to the ₹784 Cr capex spike; if the expansion underperforms, this destroys years of compounding
red_flags: FY25 revenue growth of only 8% while paying 20.8x earnings — PEG of ~1.7x on 9Y CAGR of 12% is well above my 1.0x comfort zone
FCF swung from +₹272 Cr (FY24) to −₹435 Cr (FY25) — the capex bet is now fully in play with no margin of safety if occupancy disappoints
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Nesco is what I'd call an "asset play with stalwart characteristics" — not a fast grower. The BEC is India's most prestigious exhibition venue and the IT Park delivers predictable, high-margin rental income from prime Goregaon land in Mumbai. You simply cannot replicate this asset, which is why gross margins are 85.6% and operating margins are 51%. The 9-year revenue CAGR of 12% and earnings CAGR of 11.2% are solid but unremarkable for a GARP investor paying 20.8x earnings. At a P/E of 20.8 against a 12% growth rate, the PEG of ~1.73x is above my 1.0x threshold where I get genuinely excited. The forward P/E of 17.85 implies the Street expects a meaningful earnings jump — probably from the massive ongoing expansion (CWIP jumped from ₹162 Cr to ₹761 Cr in one year, capex hit ₹784 Cr in FY25 alone).

The key question is whether this capex cycle re-accelerates growth to 20%+ as new halls and IT blocks come online, or whether the near-term revenue growth of 8% reflects real demand saturation. ROCE at 21.1% tells me management has historically allocated capital well, and the near-zero debt is a luxury most Indian companies don't enjoy. But the FCF going deeply negative (−₹435 Cr) makes this a show-me story right now. I'd want to see the new capacity driving a return to 20%+ revenue growth before paying up — current pricing assumes the best case. A patient investor could track occupancy disclosures and re-enter if the expansion proves out at a lower valuation; at ₹1,208, you're paying for success before it's delivered.
